title: Territory — Editor Intro
summary: Editorial opening splash: morning comes after the household's first night in 5B, but Gunnar still lacks the most basic orientation he trusts; clouds hide the sky while the exterior iron continues upward.
settingText: Bushwick apartment 5B, cloudy early morning

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment 5B, cloudy early morning
panelPlan.action: Full-page editorial/title splash with no conventional grid. Inside sparse apartment 5B in gray early-morning light: the brass key hangs near the door, the drafty window shows a blank overcast sky, and Gunnar stands looking upward along the exterior iron beyond the glass. Keep the room materially simple and newly occupied. Do not show a usable map, readable contact card, phone knowledge, or other modern navigation tools. The eye should travel from the locked room to the exterior iron and finally to the clouded sky above the building. Integrate the captions as deliberate editorial typography with strong hierarchy. End with Welcome to TERRITORY.

dialogueInline.text: Carrie said not to climb outside.
That is why I am going.

title: A Man on the Roof
summary: Gunnar reaches the cloudy roof and meets Silas for the first time; Silas treats him as a new neighbor while making it clear that unusual activity on the roof will not go unnoticed.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, cloudy morning

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, cloudy morning
panelPlan.action: Wide: Gunnar reaches the flat roof and finds only gray cloud, water towers, brick walls, antennas and neighboring rooftops. The sun is completely hidden.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, cloudy morning
panelPlan.action: Medium: He studies the cloud cover and horizon, dissatisfied; nothing in the sky gives him the fixed point he came for.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, cloudy morning
panelPlan.action: Wide: Silas appears from the opposite side of the roof with coffee, notices Gunnar and slows.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, cloudy morning
panelPlan.action: Two-shot: Silas keeps a neighborly distance. His tone is casual, but his curiosity is real.

dialogueInline.text: Okay. Don't screw up. I'm keeping my eye on you.
I am also keeping my eye on you.

title: The Black Glass Has an Opinion

settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, cloudy morning

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, cloudy morning
panelPlan.action: Medium: Silas notices Gunnar repeatedly checking the blank sky and asks what he is looking for.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, cloudy morning
panelPlan.action: Close: Silas takes out his phone and shows the compass screen, with the display visible only as a simple directional interface rather than readable technical detail.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, cloudy morning
panelPlan.action: Medium: Gunnar studies the device itself rather than accepting the indicated direction.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, cloudy morning
panelPlan.action: Wide: Gunnar looks back to the clouds and surrounding roofline; the phone has not solved the problem for him.

dialogueInline.text: Does the glass tell you where north is?
That's as much as I know.
The sky will tell me when it returns.
Are you planning to wait here?

title: No North Yet
summary: Gunnar returns without orientation, but his description of the roof gives Bjorn a different idea: open sky offers somewhere for smoke to go.
settingText: Bushwick apartment 5B, morning

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment 5B, morning
panelPlan.action: Wide: Gunnar climbs back through the rear window into 5B. Bjorn is awake; Astrid and the two Kin continue quiet morning tasks in the background without speaking.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment 5B, morning
panelPlan.action: Two-shot: Bjorn expects an answer about north and gets weather instead.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment 5B, morning
panelPlan.action: Medium: Gunnar describes the roof physically—open above, wind moving across it, no beams or ceiling to hold smoke.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment 5B, morning
panelPlan.action: Close on Bjorn as that last observation becomes useful for a different unresolved problem.

dialogueInline.text: The roof is open above. Wind crosses it.
Not as it does in the room.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment 5B, morning

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment 5B, morning
panelPlan.action: Medium: she notices Gunnar's damp boots and the open rear window before he closes it.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment 5B, morning
panelPlan.action: Two-shot: Gunnar states where he went without embarrassment.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment 5B, morning
panelPlan.action: Three-shot Carrie/Bjorn/Gunnar: Bjorn supplies the literal timing distinction from the previous night.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment 5B, morning
panelPlan.action: Close on Carrie as she looks at the existing DTI follow-up notice in her folder, then at the window.

dialogueInline.text: I told you not to climb outside.
The pigeon is already in your file. Do not give me today's problem before breakfast.

title: The Building's Iron
summary: The Kin begin collecting rooftop building metal for a hearth; Carrie interrupts the work and makes them restore it before a fire is lit.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, late morning

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, late morning
panelPlan.action: Carrie, Bjorn and Gunnar step from the roof access onto the tar roof. Astrid watches while the two male Kin carry loose galvanized pieces from a maintenance stack toward a proposed hearth site. Intact dish and vents remain in place.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, late morning
panelPlan.action: Carrie catches the men beside the loose pieces and points them back toward the stack; both immediately stop.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, late morning
panelPlan.action: Bjorn holds a thin loose sheet-metal piece without damaging it; Carrie points toward the working vents.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, late morning
panelPlan.action: The two male Kin return every loose piece to its original stack while Gunnar clears the proposed work area. Astrid checks that nothing remains displaced.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, late morning
panelPlan.action: Bjorn looks toward the apartment below; Carrie follows his eyeline and waits.

dialogueInline.text: They are gathering the iron for the hearth.
Put that back. It belongs to the building.
The metal is weak. It yields easily to us.
It is meant to vent air. Leave the building its air.
Then we will use something else.
You cannot build a hearth on a tar roof. It is a lease violation.
A chieftain does not forbid his people from finding warmth. It is the oldest law.

title: Winter Is Not Today
summary: Carrie finally hears the practical need beneath the hearth project: Bjorn is not cold now; he is unwilling to enter winter with only one source of warmth that nobody in the household understands or controls.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, late morning

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, late morning
panelPlan.action: Medium: the Kin silently return the last loose metal while Carrie stays with Bjorn and Gunnar.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, late morning
panelPlan.action: Two-shot Carrie/Bjorn: she asks why a spring morning has become a hearth problem.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, late morning
panelPlan.action: Medium on Gunnar: he points only toward the building below, not to any system diagram or named equipment.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, late morning
panelPlan.action: Close on Bjorn: his concern is redundancy and responsibility, not fear of modern technology.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, late morning
panelPlan.action: Wide: Carrie remains unconvinced by the solution even though the need itself is clearer.

dialogueInline.text: Why do you need a hearth in April?
We do not need it today.
Then why are we doing this today?
Because winter does not wait until you are cold to begin preparing.
The room becomes warm. We do not know how.
If it stops, we have no second fire.
Keeping the room warm is the landlord's responsibility.
And being cold would be ours.

title: The Room Is at Stake
summary: Silas documents the rooftop disturbance; Carrie explains the placement consequence, and Bjorn decides the hearth must create no trouble for anyone.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building roof, late morning

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, late morning
panelPlan.action: Silas stands at a neighboring roof edge with his phone held vertically, recording the men restoring the metal. Carrie and Bjorn notice him; Gunnar remains beside the restored stack.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, late morning
panelPlan.action: Carrie points to the restored stack, speaking toward Silas across a plausible conversational distance. Silas keeps recording.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, late morning
panelPlan.action: Carrie lowers her voice to Bjorn; Gunnar hears her beside him.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, late morning
panelPlan.action: Carrie heads for the bulkhead to make her required report. Bjorn and Gunnar stay beside the untouched roof fixtures.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building roof, late morning
panelPlan.action: Bjorn looks across the roof at the nearby windows and clear access path; Gunnar follows his survey.

dialogueInline.text: A concerned neighbor with a neighborhood watch app.
Everything is back. Nothing is damaged.
Then that is what the recording will show.
Yesterday was the fire escape. A roof complaint today can put the room under review.
The placement can be endangered without anyone burning.
Then the building's metal stays here.
And we find iron that belongs to us.
The hearth must make trouble for no one.
